questions.q: What is the standard, safe practice when a company needs to customize a seeded AAD like "Standard Accrual"?
options: Copy the seeded AAD, give the copy a clear name, and make all changes on that copy
Edit the seeded AAD directly, since it is the fastest option
Delete the seeded AAD and build a replacement with no reference material
Ask Oracle Support to modify the seeded content for you
questions.explain: Copying the seeded AAD before modifying it keeps the original intact as a reference and clearly identifies custom configuration.

questions.q: What is one risk of editing a seeded AAD directly instead of copying it first?
options: There is no risk at all; this is Oracle's recommended approach
A future Oracle patch or update that touches seeded content could overwrite or conflict with the changes
Seeded AADs cannot be read by Create Accounting
Direct edits automatically delete the ledger
questions.explain: Because seeded AADs are Oracle-owned and maintained, direct edits risk being overwritten by future patches, among other issues.

questions.q: Why do most real companies need to customize a seeded AAD rather than using it unchanged?
options: Seeded AADs are always broken and unusable out of the box
Oracle requires every company to modify seeded content before go-live
Most companies have at least some requirement the seeded definition doesn't anticipate, such as a custom supporting reference or mapping set
Seeded AADs only work for Receivables, never for other subledgers
questions.explain: Oracle cannot anticipate every company-specific need, so seeded AADs are a strong starting point that usually require some tailoring.

questions.q: If a consultant needs to change a seeded journal line rule referenced inside an AAD, what should they do?
options: Edit the seeded journal line rule directly, since it is just a smaller object than the AAD
Copy that specific rule (or the rule set containing it) rather than editing Oracle's seeded version, then point the copied AAD at the copied rule
Ignore the rule and hope it doesn't matter
Delete the rule entirely with no replacement
questions.explain: The same copy-first discipline applies at the rule level: copy a seeded rule before modifying it, rather than editing Oracle's original.

questions.q: Once a consultant is working on their own copy of an AAD, what changes are considered safe?
options: No changes are ever safe, even on a copy
Only changing the AAD's name, nothing else
Only Oracle Support is permitted to make any change, even to a copy
Adding new journal line rules, swapping in custom account rules or mapping sets, adding supporting references, or adjusting description rule wording
questions.explain: Once working on a copy, a consultant has full latitude to customize content because Oracle's original seeded version remains untouched elsewhere.
